name: allocator_v1
kind: registered allocator spec (docs/BACKLOG.md item 9): the only rule by which a forward sleeve may move into the paper account. Registered before any allocator code or result exists. Shadow first; apply stays off until the owner flips it.
question: may a DEFINED-RISK expiry-seller sleeve (an iron condor with long wings) that has earned the eligibility its own spec registered be carried overnight in the paper account, sized so one position can lose at most 2.5% of equity, without weakening any risk limit, gate or halt the desk already has

owner_decision.request: enable holding overnight positions and selling calls and puts, with right judgement
owner_decision.decision: defined risk only: iron condors / spreads with long wings. Naked selling stays a paper measurement in the sleeves (intraday/sleeves.py) and never enters the paper account.
owner_decision.real_money: off. account.mode stays paper; this spec places nothing anywhere but the paper broker and refuses to run on any other

supersedes.backlog_item_9: BACKLOG item 9 says 'per-trade max loss <= 4% of equity'. That is ABOVE the owner's ceiling (intraday.risk.risk_per_trade 0.025). This spec uses <= 2.5% and nothing looser. The 'correlation-aware, half-Kelly cap' wording of item 9 is not implemented: with at most 2 positions open and a flat 2.5% cap, a sizing rule that can only be smaller than the cap adds nothing a reviewer can check

sleeves.rule: an allocation names a sleeve of a registered expiry_seller spec, pinned by file hash. A sleeve not in this list is never allocated. A spec file whose hash differs from the pin allocates nothing (the sleeve rules it was registered under are not the rules in force).
never: any sleeve whose spec says naked: true or whose strategy is a strangle (expiry_seller_v1 B, expiry_seller_v3 D). They stay measurements

expiry_seller_v3 sleeve E: defined risk, but FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY and SENSEX are not instruments the paper account trades (the engine's underlyings are NIFTY and BANKNIFTY). A later allocator spec may add them with their own cost evidence
any underlying other than NIFTY and BANKNIFTY
sleeves.order: when several sleeves are due the same evening they are taken in the order of the allowed list, then by underlying name; each one is subject to every limit below given what the earlier ones already took

eligibility.rule: exactly the sleeve spec's own registered paper_account eligibility, evaluated by the sleeve's own assessment (intraday/sleeves.assess) on that sleeve and underlying's settled forward trades at the moment of decision: at least 10 settled forward trades, the cost check passed, the consistency check not rejected, not retired, no 'bug' recorded (a defined-risk trade that lost more than its max loss). Nothing in this spec loosens or replaces it.
stricter_additions: the sleeve must have opened a trade for this eve itself, in its own ledger, from a real-quote snapshot (source kotak or nse); the allocator never chooses strikes, deltas or an expiry: it carries out the sleeve's registered entry, legs and fills, scaled to lots

the structure is re-verified from the opened trade, not trusted from the sleeve's label: exactly four legs, one short call and one short put, each with a long wing of the same right further out of the money, wings equal in quantity to their short, every leg a quantity of one lot, the expiry the sleeve's expiry
a leg flagged locked, or a snapshot flagged late (more than 5 minutes from 15:20), refuses the allocation
eligibility.recorded: the assessment (n, cost, consistency, retired, bugs) is written into every allocator record, so a reviewer sees what was true at the moment of decision

values.shadow: DEFAULT. The allocator evaluates every rule below on the real state of the paper account and journals exactly what it WOULD place (legs, fills, lots, max loss, margin) or why it would not. It marks each shadow position with real quotes from the chain tape and records the settlement it would have had. The paper account (broker, journal trades and fills, carry registry) is not touched.
values.apply: the allocation is placed in the paper account as specified below. Effective only after at least 5 distinct sessions on which the allocator, in shadow mode, recorded a would-place allocation; with fewer recorded, apply behaves as shadow and says so in the record

mode.unknown_value: any value not listed is shadow
mode.shipping_default: shadow. The owner flips apply by hand, after reading at least 5 shadow sessions (the same shadow-then-apply pattern as intraday.learning.earn_in.mode). The engineer never does.

limits.rule: every limit is the smaller of the desk's configured value (intraday.risk.*) and the ceiling written here. The allocator can only be tighter than the desk, never looser. The configured value is read at the moment of decision.

max_loss_per_position.of: account equity at the moment of decision
max_loss_per_position.note: a flat 2.5%: the conviction scale (x0.6-1.2) the intraday sizer applies is not applied here

max_trades_per_day.note: trades opened that session, counting the allocation

max_open.note: positions open at the broker and in the journal, counting every overnight carry already held and the allocation

daily_loss.note: the session the allocation is made on must be above the limit; the allocation's max loss must fit in the day's remaining room (the intraday sizer's own C-06 rule); and the next session starts with the carry's max loss already reserved against its room

max_total_outlay.note: all open premium and blocked margin together, as a share of equity

cross_day_drawdown_halt.note: an active halt, or equity already 10% or more below the recorded peak, refuses the allocation

max_lots.note: the sleeves measured fills at one lot; two until the shadow record shows fills at size

short_legs_from_equity.note: no sold leg below that equity (the desk's own buyer-only rule); null means never sell, and then nothing is allocated

sizing.per_lot_max_loss_rupees: (wider wing width - credit) x contract lot size + entry fees + exit allowance, with every number taken from the legs as the PAPER BROKER would fill them (the sleeve's reference bid/ask, one tick worse, the broker's own fee model). Wing width = the larger of the call wing and the put wing in index points; credit = net credit in points; entry fees = the statutory fees of the four orders; exit allowance = the dated exercise STT rate x the wider wing width x lot size (an intrinsic of twice the wing on an exercised long leg).
sizing.lots: the smallest of: floor(2.5% of equity / per-lot max loss); floor(the day's remaining daily-loss room / per-lot max loss); floor(blocked-margin room / per-lot margin); floor(least size resting at the touch across the four legs / lot size) and 1 when the touch size is not recorded; max_lots; zero if any is zero. No lots means no allocation, with the binding limit named.
sizing.margin: per-lot margin = the larger of the per-lot max loss (a defined-risk position can lose no more) and intraday.risk.credit_margin_per_lot (the desk's own, stricter, SPAN-style figure). Blocked margin of the positions already open is added: debit trades at the premium paid, overnight carries at their registered margin. margin room = min(intraday.risk.max_margin, intraday.risk.max_total_outlay, 0.5) x equity - blocked.
sizing.equity: broker cash plus the open positions at cost (the same basis the intraday desk uses for the session's starting equity), never a marked-up figure

refusals.rule: ALL of the following must be clear, on the real state, or nothing is allocated (and the record says which). Checking is fail-closed: a state that cannot be read is a refusal.
list: account.mode is not paper, or the broker is not the simulated paper broker
the kill switch file is present; a new-entry pause from the app (intraday_paused); the safe mode, journal-fault or reconciliation halts the session recorded; the session's daily-loss halt
an inherited-position halt (intraday_halt) is active; a cross-day drawdown halt (intraday_drawdown_halt) is active; equity is 10% or more below the recorded peak
the risk governor stood the desk down that session (any stand-down, in any governor mode)
no session record for the day (the allocator cannot tell what the day's loss was)
the broker's positions do not equal the journal's open trades, leg for leg
any open position that is not a registered overnight carry (a stuck exit, an unexplained trade)
any limit above would be exceeded, or sizing returns no lots
the allocation is not made in the same calendar day's post-close step as the sleeve's own entry (a missed run is a missed allocation, not a late one)

placement.where: the paper broker only (intraday.sim.IntradayBroker); nothing else in the repository can place an order and this spec adds no path to one
placement.when: the post-close step that already runs the sleeves (quantdesk intraday sleeves), after the sleeve has recorded its own open for the eve. The position is timed at the sleeve's snapshot (the tape's real quotes nearest 15:20) and priced from it. It is a paper fill at recorded real quotes, placed after the session ended: it is not a live order and is not described as one.
placement.fills: sells at the recorded bid - one tick, buys at the recorded ask + one tick (the sleeve's own fill model; the broker adds its one adverse tick to the reference quote). Statutory fees per order from execution/costs.CostModel. The price the broker returns must equal the price sized on; a difference unwinds the order (below).
placement.all_or_nothing: all four legs are priced from real recorded quotes before any order is sent; a leg that cannot be priced places nothing at all.
placement.leg_order: the two long wings first, then the two short legs. A short leg is therefore always covered by a long wing that is already filled: the paper account holds no naked short option at any moment, in any order of events.
placement.failure: if any order is rejected, or returns a price other than the one sized on, the legs already filled are unwound: shorts are bought back first, then the wings are sold. Every unwind fill is journalled and its cost booked to the trade. If an unwind order itself is rejected the trade is left open and pending exit, a CRITICAL event names it, nothing is registered as a carry, and the next session's inherited-position halt stops entries for the owner. A position that is not exactly what was registered is never exempt from that halt.
placement.journal: the trade (family overnight, strategy overnight_condor_<sleeve>), its four fills with fees, and a decision row are written to the paper journal; the allocator's own ledger records the allocation and everything that follows

carry.what: an overnight carry is an allocated condor that the desk deliberately holds past the close. It exists only if it is registered (state key overnight_carry, with a fingerprint of the trade id, underlying, expiry and each leg's symbol, quantity and entry price) in the same step that placed it.
carry.rule: ONE overnight only. The carry is allowed only if the sleeve's expiry is the next trading day by the holiday calendar AND is exactly one calendar day after the eve AND the desk has a holiday list for the date (no holiday gap). A weekend or holiday between the eve and the expiry refuses the allocation. This is stricter than the sleeve's own rule (the sleeve measures eves before a weekend or a holiday); a carry over a non-trading day is never taken.
carry.square_off: the 15:15 intraday square-off, and the end-of-session close at the end of the day's run, skip a position only if it is a registered carry that still matches its registration exactly. Every other position is closed as before. The kill switch, safe mode, an owner's flatten or close from the app, and a manual close-out all still close a carry at once (risk-reducing exits are never blocked).
carry.inherited_position_halt: unchanged for everything except a registered carry. A carry is recognised, and not halted on, if and only if: its registration exists and is open; the session day is on or before its settlement day; the trade the journal holds matches the fingerprint exactly (id, strategy, underlying, expiry, every leg's symbol, quantity and entry price, no leg exited); and the broker's positions equal its legs exactly. Any difference in any of these (a leg, a quantity, a price, a day later, an extra or missing position) is treated as before: named in a CRITICAL event and entries halted until the owner clears it. A carry whose settlement day has passed unsettled is an unsettled expired position and halts. Clearing a halt remains the owner's alone.
carry.next_session: the carry is restored into the engine's open trades, counts toward max_open and the trade count, blocks another entry on the same underlying, and its max loss is its initial risk, which the intraday sizer already subtracts from the day's loss room. The session's starting equity is the carry at entry cost, so any overnight loss realised at the open counts against that day's daily-loss limit and the drawdown halt, exactly like a loss on a position opened that day.
carry.management: none. The carry is held to settlement with no stop, target or time exit, because the sleeve's registered exit rule is hold to settlement and a defined-risk position cannot lose more than its max loss. The engine's per-trade exit rules do not apply to it.

exit.rule: identical to the sleeve's registered one: cash settlement at the expiry-day settlement the sleeve itself recorded (the mean of the 15:00-15:29 one-minute closes, its fallbacks in its own order). The allocator never computes a settlement price of its own.
exit.how: in the post-close step, once the sleeve has recorded its settlement, each leg is cash-settled in the paper broker at its intrinsic value with no brokerage; a long in-the-money leg pays exercise STT at the dated costs.exercise_stt rate (the paper broker's own settle_expiry). The settlement fills are journalled, the trade is closed, the registration is closed, and the day's session state is updated so the position is not left open.
exit.unsettled: if the sleeve has no settlement the carry stays open and registered. The next session, being past the settlement day, halts on it (inherited-position halt) for the owner. Nothing guesses a price.

records.ledger: runtime/intraday/sleeves/allocator_v1.jsonl, append-only, saved with the journal: one event per allocation decision (shadow_place, refuse, place, unwind), per mark, per settlement. Never edited.
each_record: the sleeve spec hash and eligibility assessment
the mode and whether apply was effective
the limits in force (config and ceiling) and the equity, room and blocked margin used
the four legs with strikes, quantities, reference quotes and the fills sized on
lots, per-lot max loss, total max loss, margin, the binding limit
records.shadow_marks: a shadow allocation is marked with real quotes: at each later session's last chain-tape snapshot of the expiry, longs at the bid and shorts at the ask (the exit side), and finally at the sleeve's recorded settlement with the paper fee model. The result is what the position would have made had it been placed.

evidence_and_claims.no_profit_claim: this spec is risk plumbing. It claims no edge: the sleeves' own forward records are what test the edge, and with expiry_seller_v1 A NIFTY a mean of 118 rupees per lot on a standard deviation of 2232 is not distinguishable from zero in 26 trades. The allocator can lose money, within its 2.5% bound per position.
evidence_and_claims.what_shadow_shows: whether the rule would have found sleeves eligible and sized at all, how often it would have been refused and by which limit, what the allocation would have cost in fees, and how the real-quote marks and settlements compare with the sleeve's one-lot ledger. At ₹5,00,000 and a 2.5% bound, a one-lot NIFTY condor whose wings are about 150 points wide already approaches the bound; zero lots is an expected and acceptable answer.

never: a naked short option in the paper account at any moment
real money, a live order, or any broker other than the simulated paper broker
a limit looser than the desk's configured one, or looser than a ceiling above
a carry over a weekend or a holiday
a carry that is not registered, or that differs from its registration, being exempt from any halt
clearing, weakening or bypassing a halt: only the owner clears a halt
editing a registered spec, a ledger or a result, or deleting evidence
choosing a strike, delta, expiry or fill price of its own
changes: any change to these rules is a new spec (allocator_v2) with its own ledger; this file and its ledger are never edited
